disposition.title: One budget proof for each bounded Thumb path
disposition.mechanism: The compiler derives a conservative maximum guest instruction count over every path in a bounded Thumb body, including fused successors, call halfwords and folded veneers. One entry comparison selects a body with no internal budget exits. Short budgets use a private precise body. All path counts remain compile-time constants. This preserves existing timer boundaries, stop/IRQ behavior, callback state and SVC exits; it does not permit quantum overshoot. Cycles still end fusion. The implementation is generic and does not select game addresses.
disposition.native: Retired native instructions fall 2.63% in Sky Force and 0.26% in Snakes. In warmed gameplay, caller 0x801a1044 shrinks from 11,072 to 8,256 native bytes and checks its bound of 22 once at entry. This is a code-size observation, not an instruction-throughput ratio. A separate metadata-enabled capture recovers all 160 selected code versions. Of 17,998 worker samples, 1,894 have exact ARM anchors and 1,502 exact C++ anchors; 13,628 have no instruction position, 512 are outside JIT code, and 462 lack a matching snapshot. Unmapped instructions are not assigned a source by interpolation. Short-budget bodies account for 58 worker samples. The normal timing artifact disables source metadata and was reproduced with all six hashes matching after restoring its embedded revision label.
disposition.correctness: The new proof passes 32,256 state/memory/callback chain comparisons and 3,808 independent DynCom comparisons. Both games pass exact 60-frame images, guest progress, audio events and PCM. The full suite initially reports 185 passes and one failure: an old veneer test required identical generated bytes even when the new entry wrapper was present. The test now checks the preserved precise body and executes partial-ROM cases against the original behavior. Its focused rerun passes 35,280 full-state veneer cases and 288 call-boundary cases. Runtime code did not change after the full run; the other 185 checks remain applicable. The pre-existing expected harness failure and diagnostics-only skips are retained in the logs. An executed-WASM fixture counter finds 864 lower, 224 equal and 256 higher paths out of 1,344; tiny budgets pay for a cold call, so this is not a claim that every path shrinks.
disposition.decision: Adopted: Sky Force improves in all four controlled pairs. Snakes is neutral with mixed pairs. The bounded fast path is now the default for eligible Thumb entries.
disposition.interpretation: The mean Sky Force CPU gain is 2.63%; pairs range from 0.76% to 5.10%. Snakes' 0.25% mean with two faster pairs does not establish a repeatable gain. These measurements isolate the addition to the already-graduated region fusion.
disposition.policy_note: One static entry proof replaces per-instruction checks on eligible bounded Thumb paths. Precise cold recovery retains existing scheduling and single-step boundaries; no quantum overshoot is enabled.
